title: Packaging workshop: add-ons and usage limits
scratchpad:
stockroom: NOT per tech, NOT flat 129 -> 149/acct incl 1 location, +25/loc. Team+Fleet only
doorstep link = every tier (reversed!), Pay = add-on 49
photos 25GB/tech pooled (not 10), +100GB = $8
no bundle yet
on sale Tue Jan 5
Elena one-pager Fri 9th, Greta model Thu 1st
segments: Okay, let's start. This is the packaging workshop, so today is about everything that sits on top of the tiers, not the tiers themselves.
The tier prices from yesterday's review are settled, and I'm not reopening them. Today it's the add-ons and the usage limits, nothing else.
Good, because I don't think I could survive another round on tier names. I've got a short deck: three add-ons, and one page on limits at the end.
Before we dive in, can we agree that every add-on needs a margin story? I don't want things we sell at a loss just because they sound nice in a demo.
Agreed. Jun is here to tell us what each one actually costs us to run, and Elena brings what she's hearing on sales calls.
Which is mostly people asking whether things are included, honestly. Nobody likes finding a surprise line on the invoice three months in.
And for the record, every cost I quote today is a rough monthly number per account, not something to put in a spreadsheet. I'll firm them up afterwards.
Okay. Add-on one is Stockroom, the parts inventory module. Technicians see what's on their van, and the office gets a reorder list at the end of each day.
Add-on two is Doorstep, the customer portal. The homeowner gets an arrival window, a live tracking link when the technician sets off, and they can pay the invoice online.
And three is extra photo storage, which only exists as an add-on if we introduce a storage limit at all. That's the last page of the deck.
Let's take them in that order, then. Stockroom first. Marcus, what's the proposal on the slide?
Everything else we sell is priced per technician, so I kept it consistent. Stockroom at nine dollars per technician per month, available on any tier.
I have a problem with per technician for this one. Inventory doesn't scale with people. It scales with stock locations and with the size of the parts catalog.
A shop with three technicians and a big warehouse would pay twenty seven dollars a month for us to track their whole inventory. That's not a business. I'd rather charge a flat fee per account.
The counterargument is that flat fees punish the small shops. A two person outfit with one van isn't going to pay the same as a regional company with a warehouse.
From the sales side, the small shops aren't the ones asking for it. The people who ask about parts are the ones with a warehouse and a stock controller.
In the last month, I'd say nine of the demos where Stockroom came up were companies with at least one warehouse. The van-only shops didn't care at all.
Jun, what does Stockroom actually cost us to run? Is it people, parts or locations that drive the cost?
Parts, mostly. Every part in the catalog is a row we sync to every phone. A catalog of a few hundred parts is nothing. Twenty thousand parts starts to hurt.
Locations are cheap for us. Each van counts as a stock location in the current design, but that's a tiny table. The catalog size is the real cost.
So neither people nor locations really drive our cost. Which is another argument for one simple flat price per account.
Okay. What number would you put on a flat fee, Greta?
Something like a hundred and twenty nine dollars per account per month. That's roughly what a mid-sized customer would pay at Marcus's per technician price anyway.
I can live with a flat fee if it's simple to explain. One price, any number of technicians, done.
Okay, tentatively Stockroom is a hundred and twenty nine dollars a month per account, flat. Let's move on and come back to it if anything changes the picture.
Doorstep next. My proposal here was the same shape as Stockroom: five dollars per technician per month, on every tier.
That one I'd push back on hard. The tracking link is the part customers see in demos, and in my deals nobody expects to pay extra for it. It's table stakes.
Every time I show the live map of the technician driving over, the buyer asks if that's included. If I say it costs extra, it feels petty, and it colours the rest of the call.
But it isn't free to run, surely. Live tracking means location updates every few seconds while someone's driving across town.
It's cheaper than you'd think. We already collect the location during a shift for dispatch. The link just shows the homeowner one dot on a map. The cost to us is close to zero.
The expensive part of Doorstep is the payments. Taking a card means a payment processor, disputes, refunds and reconciliation. That's where the work and the risk are.
So the tracking link and the payments are really two different products with two very different cost profiles.
Then maybe the tracking link is included in Team and Fleet, and Starter doesn't get Doorstep at all. That gives people a reason to move up a tier.
I could sell that. Team buyers would see it as included, and Starter is self-serve anyway, so there's nobody on a call to complain to.
Okay, tentatively the tracking link comes with Team and Fleet, not Starter, and we price the payments part separately. Let's leave the payments number for a bit.
Can we do storage before payments? The payments number depends on what Jun says about processing costs, and storage is the one I'm actually worried about.
Sure. Jun, give us the storage picture as it stands today.
Today storage is unlimited. Technicians attach photos to jobs: before and after shots, meter readings, damage. We keep them for as long as the account is active.
Our storage bill has gone up every month this year. It's not a crisis, but it's now the third biggest line in our cloud costs, after compute and the database.
And a handful of accounts are most of it, right? I heard the roofing companies take hundreds of photos on every job.
Right. From the report I pulled, the median technician stores about three gigabytes a year. The heavy users are more like forty gigabytes a year.
So my proposal is ten gigabytes per technician included, which covers the median several times over, and then we sell extra storage in blocks.
Five dollars a month for every extra hundred gigabytes, pooled across the account so nobody has to think about who took which photo.
That sounds low to me. Do we know our own cost per hundred gigabytes, including backups and the copy in the second region?
I'd have to check the backup side before I give you a number. The primary storage alone is cheap. Backups are the part I haven't looked at.
Okay. Let me sit with that until you have it. Marcus, payments?
For Doorstep payments, I was thinking a percentage of each payment, on top of whatever the processor charges. Maybe half a percent.
I don't love percentages. Customers compare them to their bank's fees, and we end up in arguments about fractions of a percent on every renewal.
Same from sales. A flat monthly price is easier to put in a proposal. Buyers want to know the number before they sign anything.
And a percentage means we touch the money flow, which means more compliance work for Odette's team. A flat fee keeps us out of most of that.
Then Doorstep Pay is a flat add-on. What number? Greta?
Forty nine dollars per account per month feels right. It's about a third of Stockroom, and it pays for the support time that payment questions take.
Okay, Doorstep Pay at forty nine dollars a month per account. I think that one's actually settled.
And the card fees themselves? Do we pass the processor's fee straight through to the customer, or hide it inside the forty nine?
Straight through, at cost. If we bury the processor's fee in our own price, we're the ones who lose out whenever a customer has a big month.
In the setup we sketched, the processor bills the customer's own merchant account anyway. We never hold the money, which is the whole point.
Good. Card fees pass through at cost, and we never hold customer funds. Let's make sure that sentence ends up in whatever sales gets.
Can I ask a tier question about Stockroom? Is it available on Starter as well? Some Starter shops will have a small parts room.
Technically it works on any tier. But Starter accounts can only have one office location in the app, and Stockroom really wants several locations to be useful.
I'd keep Stockroom off Starter. It's a signal that you've grown into Team, and it's one more reason to upgrade.
Agreed, Stockroom is for Team and Fleet only. Starter doesn't get it.
Now, a bundle. If someone buys both Stockroom and Doorstep Pay, I'd like to offer an operations bundle at a small discount.
Say a hundred and fifty nine dollars a month for both, instead of a hundred and seventy eight separately. It gives me something to close with.
I'd rather not discount before we know anything about attach rates. If nobody buys either one, the bundle doesn't matter. If everyone buys both, we've just given money away.
There's also a messaging cost. Three add-ons and a bundle on one page is a lot for people to read before they get bored.
Let me hold the bundle question. Let's get through the limits and come back to it at the end.
Jun, what happens when an account goes over its storage? I don't want photos quietly disappearing on anyone.
Nothing gets deleted, ever. Uploads keep working. The admin sees a warning at ninety percent, and again when they cross the limit.
And billing? Do we start charging the moment they cross the line?
I'd say no. They get the rest of the month without a charge, and extra storage starts on the next invoice, with an email that explains it in plain words.
Good. A surprise charge for photos is exactly the kind of thing that ends up dominating a renewal conversation.
Okay. Over the limit, nothing's deleted, admins get warned at ninety percent, and billing for extra storage starts the following month.
Does video count? A few customers have started recording short clips of a leak or a noisy boiler instead of taking photos.
Video counts against the same pool, it's just bigger files. We compress it on upload, so a thirty second clip ends up about the size of ten photos.
I'd mention video explicitly on the page, then. Otherwise the first customer who hits the limit with clips will say nobody ever told them.
Actually, I need to correct my numbers from earlier. I had the report open while we were talking about bundles, and I read the wrong column.
The three gigabytes was per quarter, not per year. The median technician stores about twelve gigabytes a year, and the heavy ones are over a hundred and fifty.
Twelve a year. So a ten gigabyte limit would put the median technician over the line inside their first year. That's a terrible first experience.
And then everyone would be buying blocks, which turns a limit for heavy users into a tax on everybody.
The other thing I checked is the backup cost. With the copy in the second region, it's about two dollars per hundred gigabytes per month for us.
Then five dollars a block is too thin once support time is in. I'd make it eight dollars a month for each extra hundred gigabytes.
What's the included amount, then? If the median is twelve a year and photos never get deleted, we need room for at least two years.
Twenty five gigabytes per technician covers the median for about two years. The heavy users will buy blocks within the first few months, which seems fair.
Is it per technician, or pooled? If one technician takes all the photos, I don't want them hitting a wall while the rest of the account has space.
Pooled across the account. Twenty five times the number of technicians, shared by everyone on it.

Okay, let's lock it. Twenty five gigabytes per technician, pooled across the whole account, instead of the ten we started with. Extra storage is eight dollars a month for each additional hundred gigabytes.
Good. That one I can defend in a margin review.
Can we go back to Stockroom? Something Jun said about locations has been bugging me for the last twenty minutes.
One of the prospects I'm talking to has five warehouses and forty vans. At a flat hundred and twenty nine, they'd get every location for the same price as a shop with one parts room.
They told me straight out that they expected to pay per location. Their current inventory tool charges per warehouse, and they think that's normal.
That's fair. Flat per account undercharges the big multi-site customers, and they're the ones who'll lean on support the most.
And there's a cost I forgot earlier. Barcode scanning. The scanning library we'd license charges us per account, roughly eleven dollars a month each.
So at a hundred and twenty nine, eleven goes straight to the library before we've done anything. That changes the base.
What if the base includes one stock location, and every extra location costs something on top? Vans wouldn't count as locations, only warehouses and parts rooms.
That's easy to enforce. Locations are already a separate type in the data model, and vans are a different type. I'd just stop counting vans.
Then I'd move the base up to cover the scanning. A hundred and forty nine dollars a month, one stock location included, and twenty five dollars a month for each additional location.
Five warehouses would come to two hundred and forty nine a month. That's right in the range they told me they expected.
And the shop with one parts room still pays the base. I'm fine with that. It's still one number on the pricing page for most people.

Okay, final for Stockroom. A hundred and forty nine dollars per account per month, including one stock location, plus twenty five dollars a month for each additional location, Team and Fleet only. That replaces both the per technician idea and the flat hundred and twenty nine.
Agreed. That's the version I'll put in the model.
I want to reopen one thing on Doorstep. Leaving Starter without the tracking link has been bothering me since we said it.
Starter is exactly the small shops who want to look professional. A tracking link is the cheapest thing we could give them that makes them look bigger than they are.
And it costs us next to nothing, like I said. The tracking link is a page and a dot on a map. Holding it back from Starter saves us nothing at all.
From sales, Starter is self-serve, so it's not really my fight. But if it makes Starter convert better, those shops grow into Team later anyway.
My only condition is that payments stay paid. The tracking link can go everywhere, but Doorstep Pay stays an add-on.

Then let's reverse the earlier call. The Doorstep tracking link is included in every tier, Starter included. Doorstep Pay, the online invoice payments, stays an add-on at forty nine dollars a month per account.
Thank you. That's also a much simpler sentence for the pricing page.
Back to the bundle, Elena. With the new Stockroom price, does it still make sense to you?
Honestly, less than before. With per location pricing, the bundle would need its own location rules. That's a lot of fine print for a small discount.
Then no bundle for now. Let's watch real attach rates for a quarter, and if most Stockroom buyers also take Doorstep Pay, we can talk about a bundle then.
Agreed. No bundle at the start. We revisit it once we have a quarter of real data.
When do these actually go on sale? My prospects are going to ask me that before anything else.
Not in the same week as the new tiers, please. I don't want three new things on the page while people are still reading the tier names.
Engineering-wise, Stockroom's scanning needs the library contract signed, and the storage meter for admins doesn't exist yet. December at the earliest, realistically.
Then the add-ons go on sale on Tuesday the fifth of January. Everybody, plan to that date, and tell me early if it's at risk.
Owners. Marcus, the add-ons need a product page, and sales needs a one-pager they can send after a demo.
I can do both. The one-pager by next Wednesday, the thirtieth, and the page after that.
Hang on. You've got the tier page this month, and that one has a real deadline on it. I don't want the add-on work slowing that down.
I'll take the sales one-pager. I'm the one who'll use it most, and I know which questions come up on calls.
But not by the thirtieth, I've got customer prep all next week. I'll have the add-on one-pager for sales done by Friday the ninth of October.
The ninth is fine. Nobody's selling these before January anyway. Marcus keeps the product page, for December.
I'll update the revenue model with today's prices and some attach rate assumptions, and send it round by Thursday the first of October.
And I'll get the storage meter and the ninety percent warning into the admin page before the fifth of January. Teodor can probably pick most of it up.
One more for the page. Do we show the extra location price on the public page, or only in a quote?
On the public page. If the number's hidden, people assume it's bigger than it is.
Public page, then. Okay, let me recap so the notes are right.

Stockroom is a hundred and forty nine a month per account with one stock location, plus twenty five per extra location, Team and Fleet only. The Doorstep tracking link is in every tier, and Doorstep Pay is forty nine a month.
Storage is twenty five gigabytes per technician, pooled, with extra hundred gigabyte blocks at eight dollars a month. No bundle yet. Everything goes on sale on the fifth of January.
That matches my notes. The one-pager from me on the ninth, and Greta's model on the first.
And I'll flag anything in the model that looks off before anyone quotes these numbers to a customer.
Perfect. Thanks everyone, that was a lot of numbers for one afternoon.

items.text: Stockroom priced at $149 per account per month including one stock location, plus $25 per additional location; Team and Fleet only (replaces $9 per technician and the flat $129)
Doorstep tracking link included in every tier, Starter included (reverses the Team-and-Fleet-only call); Doorstep Pay is an add-on at $49 per account per month
Photo storage: 25 GB per technician pooled across the account (not 10 GB); extra storage $8 per month per 100 GB; nothing is ever deleted over the limit
No add-on bundle at the start; revisit after a quarter of attach rate data
Add-ons go on sale on Tuesday, January 5
Write the add-on one-pager for sales by Friday, October 9
Update the revenue model with the add-on prices and attach rate assumptions by Thursday, October 1
Add the storage meter and 90% warning to the admin page before January 5
